question: The angle of elevation of the top of a small tree from a point on the ground 300 m away from the foot of the tree was 30°. When the tree grew taller, its angle of elevation became 60° from the same point. By how much did the tree grow?
solution:
**Given:**

Angle of elevation initially (θ₁) = 30°

Angle of elevation after growth (θ₂) = 60°

Distance from the point on the ground to the foot of the tree (d) = 300 m

**Formula used:**

Height of the tree (h) = d × tan(θ)

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1bfc98d45034cef89fb867cf031be4c6995080b6720e87a6131860d3363c2fa2.png] 

Initial height of the tree (h₁):

h₁ = 300 × tan(30°)

⇒ h₁ = 300 × 1/√3

⇒ h₁ = 300/√3

Height of the tree after growth (h₂):

h₂ = 300 × tan(60°)

⇒ h₂ = 300 × √3

⇒ h₂ = 300√3

Increase in height (h₂ - h₁):

⇒ 300√3 - 300/√3

⇒ 300(√3 - 1/√3)

⇒ 300((3 - 1)/(√3))

⇒ 300(2/√3) = (600 × √3) / 3

 ⇒ 200√3

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**
